record_notes.DCP-LETT-1045: Friday assigned January–August 1848. Note received yesterday, specimen box this morning: distinct events, no exact calendar receipt day from this broad range. First monograph-intention mention December 18, 1847 and Quekett contact September 7, 1848 provide editorial rationale but do not strictly exclude intervening Fridays December 24/31 or September 1 outside encoded range. Preserve inferred period rather than silently extending. Acasta shell study now possible; old shabby specimen only almost surely a new genus. Later Pachylasma identification and systematic relationships are editorial hindsight. Wet Acasta requested, not already possessed. Quekett introduction requested because not acquainted; no accomplished introduction or preserved Bowerbank note.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1229: February 24 with supplied 1849 year. Scalpellum fragments, Plumularia and sufficient Acasta specimens received. Acasta seem new but Darwin explicitly says he knows nothing of genus as yet; do not infer completed systematic study from specimen possession. Plumularia return promised later, fulfilled or renewed by 1305A a year later. Malvern trip intended for April and two months; actual March departure and sixteen-week stay are later outcomes. No incoming Bowerbank cover survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1294: January 19 with supplied 1850 year. Earlier missing permission acted on: large valve cleared and four embedded pieces separated, with three valves still in position. Offer of sessile specimens acknowledged, not yet ready for their study. Missing Forbes letter reports possible Gault Pollicipes at Bowerbank; older Forbes shell/depth manuscripts do not match. New permission to have Sowerby draw requested, distinct from already granted cleaning permission. Fitch specimens received. Copenhagen fossils still hoped for immediately, not yet arrived. Palaeontographical publication proposal still under consideration and sequencing uncertain; later acceptance not backdated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1296: Thursday assigned January 24–March 7, 1850, conditional on probable Bowerbank recipient and sequence relative to 1294/1310. Recipient is not certain; do not force participants.q for future transcript. Fossil Balani safely received, systematic study future. Lubbock recruited to your Society, whose identity is unresolved: Palaeontographical membership already listed in 1848, whereas Ray Society subscription fits 1849–1851. That conflict limits the inferred dating rationale; no new precise day or definitive society chosen. Missing cover cannot be reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1305A: February 25 with supplied 1850 year supported by cancellation-code window and damaged February 26 postmark. Found dry/spirit sponges, offers them and intends leaving at Geological Society next Thursday, February 28, not proof actual dispatch or personal London visit. Further specimens believed present but cannot be found. Plumularia return statement refers specimen acknowledged in 1229, same-author loan continuity rather than QA. Later June 1851 request to re-examine remains future. Bowerbank later monograph and absent acknowledgment do not negate historical gift.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1310: Friday evening conjectured March 8, 1850 from March 17 follow-up; apparatus excludes March 15 only as probably insufficient time for response, not logically impossible. Exact-date hold retained. Misdirected missing letter travelled via Farnham and arrived yesterday; do not turn relative day into securely March 7. Loan specimen includes presumed new Chthamalus and B. cranchii; later taxonomy remains separate. Offers purchase or retention as loan, payment completed only by later 1312 stamps. Society acceptance now heard, drawings/MS still being prepared. Copper engraving required for growth lines; Sowerby drawing already under way but engraving preference not completed commission. Hanley address still requested; membership only supposed, not proved admission.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1312: March 17 with supplied 1850 year independently supported by copyist-recorded March 18 postmark. Missing Bowerbank response supplies Hanley address requested in 1310. Visit to Hanley prospective when next in London, not accomplished here. Enclosed stamps pay for Eling specimen, resolving earlier loan/purchase option, but no actual delivery of stamps or Hanley meeting inferred. Logistics is eligible correspondence in principle, but missing prompt precludes pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1382F: Wednesday assigned April 24, 1850 from council meeting Friday April 26. Circular received this morning announces meeting, does not grant permission. Requests eight foreign species openly included in small type, supported by reported oral views of Forbes, Morris and Flower; actual April 26 funding/permission in minutes is later editorial outcome. Sponge bottle sent last Thursday, April 18 under assigned date; recipient receipt explicitly queried, not established. Charlesworth report of Pearce recovery is attributed historical information; Darwin approach to Pearce unanswered and fossil examination not done. Preserve current concinus spelling, separately note later concinnus if needed. No circular, Charlesworth communication or Pearce response text survives here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-866: Pinned prior full primary reading reused for substantive negative comparison. Friday9May inferred from13May reply. Incoming fragment says lists examined yesterday, depths provisionally marked from generic associations, needs average sizes, abundance and preservation for each locality; Huafo depth could double under stated conditions. Marked lists are at separate manuscript reference, not transcribed here. No insect discussion. Supports867P1 response declining additional data; list request from Darwin missing.
